rationale: rule:prospecting_default

Near-term intent is clear (packaging project starting in eight weeks, wants commercial info this week) and the drawing allows several optical technologies, but spend level and the signer for component purchases are unknown.

There is near-term intent (project starting in eight weeks) and no technical or certification blocker, but the engineer cannot state the budget or who signs component purchases, and the founder has disengaged; in machine building the specifier and the approver are usually different people.
rule:technical_review_with_incumbent

Budget, purchasing contact, price and delivery are all settled, but the open question is whether the sensor's wetted materials tolerate the new cleaning liquid; the engineer can supply composition, concentration and temperature in writing, so a document-based compatibility review is the right next step.

Chemical compatibility of the wetted parts with the new cleaning liquid is unconfirmed, and per the PT/PC records compatibility must be checked per application from the customer's written medium, concentration and temperature data, which the engineer can supply; budget, contact, price and delivery are already settled.
rule:trust_concern_with_incumbent_late

Specs (interface, resolution, mounting) and price/delivery are agreed, and there is an incumbent with unreliable shipments motivating a switch, but the engineer doubts performance stability during real winding cycles and management will not convert all encoders at once — a limited trial on the one available machine addresses the product-performance risk.

Specs (interface, resolution, mounting) are signed off and price/delivery accepted, with a clear switch motive (unreliable incumbent shipments); the only remaining concern is unproven performance during winding cycles, and the customer can free one machine for a limited trial rather than a full changeover.
rule:trust_concern

Budget is set and the published range fits the application, so the only remaining barrier is her doubt about our experience serving ceramic equipment makers; credibility must be established before any trial, and she has not agreed to provide equipment for evaluation.

The only objection is doubt that we have served ceramic equipment makers and understand their servicing expectations — a supplier-credibility concern, not a product-performance one — and she has not offered equipment for a trial, so trust must be built first.
rule:supplier_audit_required

Specs, price and delivery are agreed and budget approved; the only remaining barrier is the customer's supplier admission procedure requiring an on-site audit of calibration and traceability, which explicitly cannot be satisfied by document review, and the quality manager has availability next month.

Specs, budget, pricing and delivery are all settled; the only remaining barrier is the customer's supplier admission procedure requiring an in-person audit of calibration and traceability at our premises, which documents cannot replace, and the quality manager has availability next month.
rule:price_objection_late_stage

Validation is complete and delivery, warranty and payment terms are accepted, so the only remaining barrier is the owner's demand for a 12 percent discount, which she will not trade against smaller lot sizes; the decision maker is the owner herself with a near-term order date.
Validation is complete and terms are accepted, so price is the only remaining barrier; the requested 12 percent discount exceeds the 5 percent sales authority and requires sales director approval.
rule:prospecting_default

Fit is confirmed (housing and electrical interface match the planned design) but both engineering and purchasing state no buying or supplier change until the redesign in eighteen months, so there is a genuine future opportunity with no near-term intent.

Fit is confirmed (housing and electrical interface match) but the customer explicitly will not buy or switch suppliers until the redesign in eighteen months, which matches the 12-24 month design cycle pattern; this is a future opportunity, not a mismatch.
rule:qualifying_default

The fixed mounting space requires a custom housing since no catalogue standard fits, yet the total demand is a one-time four units with explicitly no follow-on volume, which is far below any viable threshold for custom tooling; flexible timing will not change this.

The application requires a custom housing, but only four units are needed and no further units ever will be, far below the non-negotiable 300-unit minimum for custom housings, which cannot be combined with other orders; no standard housing fits the fixed mounting space.
rule:budget_or_authority_unclear

Specs appear to match and price is acceptable, and the engineer states a replacement must happen within six weeks, but funding source balance and release authority are unknown and the purchasing manager who signs orders has not responded, with conflicting budget-freeze signals from finance.

Specs and price appear acceptable and the engineer needs a replacement within six weeks, but the only open barrier is which budget applies and who can release it — the engineer claims a separate maintenance account without knowing its balance or approver, and the order-signing purchasing manager has not responded.
rule:prospecting_default

Budget, decision team and timeline are settled and commercial terms are unquestioned, but fit is unconfirmed for polished, curved, moving targets, and engineering will not accept catalogue figures; the customer can supply reflectivity data, drawings, speed profiles and tolerances electronically, so a document-based spec review is the right next step.

Budget, decision team and timing are settled, but the technical fit is still open: repeatability is specified only for flat matte targets at rest, and performance on the customer's polished, curved, moving workpieces must be determined from reflectivity, drawings and speed profiles, which the customer can supply electronically so no on-site assessment is needed.
rule:trust_concern_with_incumbent_late

Specs, commercial terms, budget and supplier qualification are all settled, and the only open issue is unproven sustained performance on dusty produce in their own process — with an idle spare lane and purchasing able to authorize a small quantity, a limited trial addresses the product-performance risk.

Specs, commercial terms, budget and supplier qualification are all settled; the only open issue is production staff doubt about sustained performance on dusty produce, and an idle sorting lane plus purchasing authority for a small quantity make a limited trial the natural next step.
rule:trust_concern

Specs and price are acceptable and funding/decision makers are in place, but management doubts our credibility in laundry machinery and explicitly blocks evaluation resources until comparable-industry references are provided.

Specs are considered suitable and budget/roles are set, but management doubts our experience in laundry machinery and explicitly blocks any evaluation resources until references from comparable companies are provided, so trust must be established before a trial.
rule:technical_review_with_incumbent

Specs (interface, measurement range) already match, but the remaining open item — mounting clearance and cable route behind a moving guard — can only be assessed physically at the running machine, and the plant permits escorted engineers in a maintenance window in three weeks.

Specs (interface, range) match and commercial terms are accepted, but the remaining open item is mounting clearance and cable routing behind a moving guard that can only be measured at the running machine during the maintenance window in three weeks.
rule:price_objection_late_stage

All technical, quality, delivery and terms issues are closed and authority is confirmed; the only remaining barrier is an explicit demand for a 14% price reduction that exceeds normal seller discount authority, with a one-week deadline before the board award.

Technical acceptance, supplier approval, delivery and payment terms are all complete, leaving price as the only barrier; the required 14 percent reduction far exceeds the 5 percent sales authority and the customer has already exhausted volume, packaging and shipment trade-offs, with a board deadline in place.
rule:no_near_term_plan

Product fit is confirmed and there is genuine future interest for the next design generation, but an exclusive incumbent agreement runs for eleven more months and both managers have stated in writing that no transaction will occur before then; the opportunity is real but not near-term.

Fit is confirmed technically, but an exclusive agreement runs for eleven more months and both managers have ruled out any transaction until it expires, with detailed design of the next generation starting about two months later — a clear future opportunity, not a mismatch.
rule:technical_review_default

The frozen customer specification demands continuous sensor-head operation at 420 degrees Celsius in a sealed space with no option for remote mounting, a protective sleeve, or any change to temperature or envelope, so the requirement is a fixed hard limit far beyond a standard embedded sensor head rather than an open fit question that time or negotiation could resolve.

The frozen specification requires continuous sensor head operation at 420 °C, but the TS series tops out at 180 °C with no higher-temperature version existing or planned, and the sealed space rules out remote mounting or sleeves, so this is a hard specification mismatch that time will not resolve.
rule:proposal_default

Technical fit and delivery are accepted with near-term intent (production in ten weeks), but it is unknown whether the integrator's purchasing or the OEM's central team will issue the order and no spending allocation is confirmed, and the approving engineer has no purchasing authority.

Technical fit and delivery are already accepted with near-term intent (production in ten weeks), but it is unsettled whether the integrator or the manufacturer's central team will order and no spending allocation is confirmed, and the approving engineer has no purchasing authority.
rule:qualifying_default

Budget, timing and price are settled, but the product fit is unconfirmed because startup pressure peaks and repeated overload duration are missing; the customer can send logs and drawings electronically, so a document-based spec review suffices rather than a site visit.

Budget, timing and price are settled, but the startup pressure peaks and repeated overload duration are unknown, and the PC series service life depends on peaks staying within the 1.5x overload limit; the customer can supply logs and drawings electronically, so a document review resolves the open fit question.
rule:negotiation_default

Specs, price and terms are agreed and the incumbent is discontinuing the housing (switch motive), but operators fear unexpected stops over a full shift — a product performance risk that a limited initial run on the available isolated line can resolve, since funds and authority exist for that quantity.

Specs, price and terms are agreed and there is a clear switch motive (incumbent discontinuing the housing), but the remaining barrier is product-performance doubt about stability over a full shift; an isolated line and funds for a limited quantity make a small initial order the right step.
rule:technical_review_default

Specs and funding are already accepted; the sole remaining barrier is the operations director's belief that we only serve laboratory equipment firms and lack continuous-production experience, and she has blocked machine time — so credibility in comparable paper converting plants must be established before any trial or on-site work.

Specs and funding are already accepted; the only barrier is the operations director's belief that we serve only laboratory equipment customers and lack understanding of continuous paper-converting production, and she has blocked machine time so no trial or on-site assessment is possible yet. Sector-comparable references must establish credibility first.
rule:supplier_audit_required

Interface and measurement range are already accepted and budget is approved, so the only remaining barrier is the customer's mandatory supplier qualification audit witnessed on site, which explicitly cannot be satisfied by photos or a video call.

Specs and budget are accepted; the only barrier is a mandatory supplier qualification audit that the medium customer's quality policy requires to be witnessed on our premises, and documents or video are explicitly not accepted.
rule:price_objection_late_stage

All technical, approval, payment and delivery items are settled; the only remaining barrier is an explicit 8% price gap (92 vs 100) that the buyer will not trade against service or shipping concessions, on a 6,000-unit funded annual volume.

All technical, approval, payment and delivery matters are closed and the only barrier is an 8 percent discount request (92 vs 100), which exceeds the 5 percent sales authority and needs the sales director; the buyer has already ruled out trading service or shipping terms.
rule:technical_review_default

Technical fit is confirmed and we are an approved supplier with drawings retained for restart, but the board postponed the platform and both programme director and purchasing head confirm no component buying for at least nine months — a future opportunity with no near-term purchase plan.

Product fit and supplier approval are confirmed with no incumbent, but the machine platform is postponed and both the programme director and purchasing head confirm no component purchases for at least nine months; engineering retains the approved drawings for restart, so the opportunity remains for the future.
rule:prospecting_default

The signed engineering requirement mandates the controller vendor's proprietary protocol with no converters allowed and no ability to change the controller, a hard interface requirement our sensors cannot meet; budget and timing do not resolve this mismatch.

The customer's signed requirement permits only the controller vendor's proprietary protocol with no gateways allowed, while the LP linear position series supports only SSI, IO-Link and analog and the company offers no proprietary protocol support, gateways or custom firmware; this is a hard specification mismatch that time cannot resolve.
rule:negotiation_default

Specs and price are accepted, but there is a direct conflict between the purchasing contact's claim of verbal owner approval and the owner's statement that capital spending is suspended, with no documented approval or spare-parts exemption; budget authority must be confirmed before an order.

Specifications and price are already accepted, so the only open barrier is authority/budget: the purchasing contact claims the owner verbally approved and that the sensors are spare parts outside the freeze, but the owner states capital spending is suspended and no approval record exists. On money matters the owner's statement prevails and the applicable budget category must be confirmed with him.
rule:no_objection_late_stage

Commercial terms (budget, authority, price, delivery) are settled, but there is an unresolved 50 vs 12,000 mPa·s viscosity discrepancy that determines whether the flow sensor fits; the engineer is sending fluid and temperature records, so a document-based spec review is the right next step rather than ordering.

Commercial terms are settled, but the requirement sheet (50 mPa·s) and the later process note (12,000 mPa·s) conflict, and the FL series gives no usable signal above 2,000 mPa·s, so product fit is unconfirmed until the engineer's fluid and temperature records are reviewed.
rule:trust_concern

Specs were fully verified and signed off, terms accepted, and the owner has funds and authority for a limited quantity; the only remaining concern is product performance risk (counting stability during repeated starts/stops) versus an incumbent that is hard to obtain, and a spare machine is available for a trial.

Specs, signal, speed and resolution are signed off and terms accepted, and the only remaining concern is product behavior (counting stability during repeated starts) with an incumbent supply problem as switch motive; the owner can approve a limited quantity and has a spare machine for a trial.
rule:proposal_default

The only remaining barrier is the owner's doubt that we have experience in dusty cutting workshops rather than electronics assembly; spec, price, delivery and paperwork are accepted, and he will not commit technician or machine time (so no pilot or site visit) until trust in sector experience is established.

The only remaining barrier is doubt about our supplier experience in dusty cutting workshops, and the owner won't commit technician or machine time until that trust is established; spec, price and delivery are already accepted, so evidence from comparable cutting-application customers is the right next step.
rule:budget_or_authority_unclear

Specs and price are accepted with funding in place, but the large customer's quality rule mandates an on-site audit of our production line and serial-number traceability, which certificates cannot waive, so supplier qualification via site visit is the remaining barrier.

Specs and price are accepted and funding exists; the only remaining barrier is the customer's mandatory supplier qualification audit at our premises to observe production and serial-number traceability, which certificates cannot waive.
rule:price_objection_late_stage

Technical fit, approvals and all commercial terms are accepted, leaving an explicit 9% price reduction as the only remaining barrier, and the customer rules out spec, volume or logistics trade-offs, so the discount must be escalated beyond the seller's authority.

Technical acceptance, approval and commercial terms are all settled, leaving only the price gap: the required nine percent discount exceeds the 5 percent sales authority, and the owner has ruled out volume, spec or shipment trade-offs.
rule:negotiation_default

Technical and commercial terms are already agreed and our product remains on the approved list, but the machine programme is postponed twelve months and the purchase date was withdrawn with no interim component or stock need — a future opportunity that only time resolves.

Terms and specs are agreed and our product remains on the approved supplier list, but the machine programme is postponed twelve months and both owner and purchasing have withdrawn the purchase date with no interim need, so there is a future but not near-term opportunity.
rule:technical_review_with_incumbent

The design imposes a hard, non-negotiable requirement (true battery-free absolute position after power loss, no homing, no controller changes) and product fit has not yet been confirmed, even though budget, volume and delivery date are already known.

The finalized design hard-requires absolute position after power loss with no homing and no battery backup, but the supplier's RE series is incremental only with no absolute version planned or accessory that retains position — an unchangeable mismatch, not a timing issue.
rule:budget_or_authority_unclear

Technical acceptance is complete and terms are acceptable with a seven-week need date, so the only open issue is that neither division owns the component budget, no purchasing signer is identified, and finance has received no funding request.

Technical acceptance is done and there is near-term intent (parts needed in seven weeks) with acceptable pricing, but neither division owns the component budget, no purchasing manager is identified, and finance has no funding request.
rule:price_objection_late_stage

A new hotter cleaning cycle conflicts with the accepted specification and no one has confirmed which revision governs, so temperature fit is an open technical question that must be resolved (via the electronically available cycle record) before price negotiation or order; price is therefore not the only remaining barrier.

A hotter cleaning cycle was added after the accepted specification and nobody has confirmed which temperature revision governs, so product fit is open; the engineer can transmit the cycle record electronically, making a document review sufficient. The 10 percent request would exceed the 5 percent discount authority, but price is not the only remaining barrier, so escalation is premature.
rule:trust_concern_with_incumbent_late

Specs and terms are accepted, there is an incumbent with delayed parts as switch motive, and the clarified objection is whether detection stays consistent in dusty shifts on the customer's own line — a product performance risk. Funds, a separate production cell and authority for a limited quantity exist, and management requires operating evidence before full changeover.

Specifications and terms are accepted and the switch motive (incumbent delays) is clear; the remaining doubt is product performance—detection consistency in dusty shifts on the customer's own line—and funds, a separate production cell and authority for a limited quantity exist, so a small trial run supplies the operating evidence management requires.
rule:trust_concern_with_incumbent_late

Specs, price and delivery are already accepted; the only remaining barrier is management's doubt about our track record with battery machinery customers, and the operations director will not fund or schedule any product evaluation until that reference history is proven.

Specs, price and delivery are already accepted; the gating barrier is management's doubt about our track record with battery machinery businesses, and the operations director will not release machine time or funds for a product trial until that supplier-level doubt is answered.
rule:negotiation_default

All commercial and technical terms are settled, but the quality head who signs supplier admission requires witnessing calibration handling on premises, so a document review is insufficient and the audit is the only remaining barrier.

All technical and commercial terms are agreed, but the medium customer's quality head—who signs supplier admissions—requires witnessing calibration handling at our premises before final admission, and purchasing cannot order without it; documents alone do not substitute.
rule:qualifying_default

Engineering and quality approvals are complete and the buyer accepts warranty, payment and delivery terms, so the only remaining barrier is the required 13 percent reduction to meet the approved component allowance — a discount level beyond normal seller authority for a 22,000 unit/year award.

Engineering and quality approvals are done and warranty, payment and delivery terms are accepted, so the sole remaining barrier is the buyer's required 13 percent reduction to meet the component allowance — far above the 5 percent sales discount authority, and the buyer can award the 22,000-unit order once price fits.
rule:prospecting_default

The programme director and purchasing head confirmed this week that the feature is deferred fifteen months with no parts or evaluation spend authorized, so there is no near-term purchase despite the engineer's stale 'urgent' emails; the published spec fits, so the opportunity remains for later.

The programme director and purchasing head confirmed the feature is deferred 15 months with no parts or evaluation spend authorized, and machine-builder design cycles mean the order comes when detailed design starts; the fit is good, so this is a future opportunity rather than a disqualification, and the engineer's 'urgent' emails do not override the authoritative deferral.
rule:hard_requirement_unmet

The buyer has a concrete, non-negotiable hard requirement (independent hygienic certification for wetted assemblies) plus budget and ~600 units/year, but the scenario never establishes whether our sensor holds that certification, so product fit must be verified against the spec before any trial or disqualification.

The end customer's signed spec requires independent third-party hygienic certification for wetted sensor assemblies and will not accept a manufacturer's declaration, while the LV series and the company hold no such certification and have no programme to obtain one — an unmeetable hard requirement.
